# 3.2.x Vulcanus discovery recovery preparation

This disposable three-stage fixture keeps the single `mir-fixture-discovery-recovery` identity while a published MIR 3.2.0 or 3.2.1 source save is handed to MIR5 on official Factorio 2.1.23 Space Age. The source validates the emitted historical iron row, including its exact unordered `iron-plate` and `casting-iron` productivity vector. For 3.2.0 it requires the one retained `planet-discovery-vulcanus` travel effect and observes a researched discovery with Vulcanus naturally locked after the actual source lab. For 3.2.1 it requires the official ordered `unlock-space-location` Vulcanus and travel effects and observes the naturally unlocked result after that lab. It retains the source iron formula and time unchanged, accelerating only the source discovery lab. The MIR5 successor validates its current iron row and accelerates only that candidate lab to one count and five seconds. It labels only direct prerequisite seeds, then scripts the independent MIR iron level-three/42-percent queue witness. It does not insert an unlock effect or call `lock_space_location` to manufacture either source state. Those scripted iron values are fixture state, not published defaults or an observation of the historical defect.

The source also creates a separate foreign force with unresearched locked Vulcanus and a 27-percent iron queue. Before it creates a laboratory or writes successor storage, the MIR5 successor preserves the protected source state and foreign lock, both iron queues, the player level-three 20-percent iron-plate contribution, saved-progress domain/value, and the protected same-mod fixture state. The 3.2.0 successor route additionally requires ordinary MIR recovery to restore its researched player location; the fresh 3.2.1 route is a no-repair retention control and cannot show that a 3.2.0-to-3.2.1 handoff repaired an inherited lock. It then proves supplied science was consumed by one current iron laboratory, saves, and requires two read-only cold reload observations.

The 3.2.0 wrapper deliberately refuses if its actual emitted `planet-discovery-vulcanus` row is absent or has the wrong retained effect. Historical evidence records that a 3.2.0 external discovery target could be pruned; this fixture never recreates, unhides, or substitutes that prototype to force an input through. The 3.2.1 wrapper likewise refuses a missing or wrong Vulcanus unlock effect. Both routes remain prepared source inputs until their exact packages, engine executions, source saves, successor runs, and two reloads are independently captured.

Each stage is a five-member caller-composed fixture projection: the stage `info.json`, `control.lua`, and `data-final-fixes.lua`, plus the shared `fixture_control.lua` and `fixture_data_final.lua`. The forthcoming R04 prepared-input record will pin the reviewed raw source, owned archives, eight-mod selections and a private proposed-helper package without changing this fixture's scope. Its separate a575 control observes whether the engine itself restores discovery; a control pass cannot establish that the helper ran or was necessary. Source-save hashes remain unbound, and Black Glass retains native scheduling and exclusive library ownership. This preparation does not qualify a full 3.2 catalogue, ordinary science tuning, historical bug cause, performance, Library behavior, multiplayer, or release readiness.
